hints: Try it with just 3 points first — how many segments can you draw between them?
Each point pairs with every other point once. That's n(n-1) ordered pairs, but each segment gets counted twice (once from each end), so divide by 2.

canonical: Every pair of the 4 points gives one line segment, and order doesn't matter — the segment from point 1 to point 2 is the same segment as from point 2 to point 1.
The number of pairs from 4 points is n(n-1)/2 = 4(4-1)/2.

stem: 4 points are marked on a straight line, no two in the same place. Counting every pair of these points as the two endpoints of a line segment, how many different line segments do the 4 points determine in total?
